results.title: Swimming with Gaza: Palestinian children take swimming lessons in the Mediterranean
results.content: Scores of Palestinian children gathered on Friday along Gaza's Mediterranean coast in Khan Younis, exercising on the sand before heading into the water for swimming lessons.

results.title: African negotiators at COP31 demand concrete measures on climate justice
results.content: The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN) called for concrete measures on climate justice at COP31, as the UN climate talks went into overtime on Friday.

results.title: Nigerian-Ghanaian chef travels Africa to preserve culinary heritage
results.content: For the Benga community, razor clams are more than a source of food. They represent a cultural legacy passed down through generations

results.title: Turkey: Activists chant 'shame' as COP31 negotiations falter
results.content: Climate activists denounced the proposed outcome of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday 20 November 2026, accusing governments of failing to deliver meaningful progress on tackling climate change. They chanted "shame" as negotiations approached their deadline.

results.title: Italy: Workers and students stage nationwide strike over living costs
results.content: Workers and students marched through Rome, on Friday 20 November 2026, joining a nationwide strike over stagnant wages, rising living costs and government spending priorities. Protesters also demanded more funding for education and criticised military spending.

results.title: Lebanese journalist injured in Israeli strike receives CPJ Press Freedom Award
results.content: AFP journalist Christina Assi, who lost a leg in an Israeli strike reporting from the Lebanese border and has become a vocal campaigner for reporters' safety, is honoured by the Committee to Protect Journalists.

results.title: Ukraine: Rescue teams search wreckage after deadly Russian strike on Kyiv
results.content: A Russian overnight attack on Kyiv, Ukraine, killed eight people on Friday 20 November 2026, according to Associated Press, leaving buildings and warehouses damaged across the capital. Firefighters battled blazes as emergency crews searched the wreckage and police collected evidence.

results.title: South Africa's murder rate falls but killings average 60 a day
results.content: South Africa recorded fewer murders between July and September with 5,590 people killed, continuing a downward trend in violent crime, the police ministry said on Friday. The country's murder rate still averages 60 a day.

results.title: Myanmar rejects ICJ Rohingya genocide ruling as 'unfair'
results.content: Myanmar's government on Thursday rejected an International Court of Justice ruling holding the country responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, calling the decision unfair.

results.title: Activists protest failure of COP31 to advance on moving away from fossil fuels
results.content: Civil society groups and activists on Friday protested against UN climate talks' failure to advance ideas to move away from fossils fuels.

results.title: Tunisian rights activist Sihem Bensedrine sentenced to 5 years in prison
results.content: Tunisian rights activist Sihem Bensedrine has been sentenced to five years in prison by the country’s criminal chamber for financial corruption.

results.title: UK anthem returns to the EU stage in symbolic post-Brexit moment
results.content: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was welcomed by EU leaders in Brussels for a summit aimed at strengthening post-Brexit relations. God Save the King rang out for the first time since Brexit at the UK–EU summit.

results.title: Falz joins designers and models on runway at Lagos fashion showcase
results.content: Among the highlights was Oshobor Peter's collection, titled "A Different Kind of Human", which embraced maximalism through bold colours, striking shapes and expressive silhouettes.

results.title: Christmas tree up in Vatican's St Peter's Square ahead of December lighting
results.content: A 25-metre-tall silver fir will be accompanied by a life-size nativity scene and be decorated with clay ornaments and 50,000 smart LED lights.

results.title: Vatican: Giant Christmas tree lifted into place beside St Peter's Basilica
results.content: A towering 25-metre Christmas tree was lifted into place in St Peter's Square, Vatican City, on Friday 20 November 2026, as preparations began for this year's Christmas celebrations. The silver fir, donated by a community in southern Italy, will be unveiled on 7 December.

results.title: Benin requests return of 35 looted artifacts from Paris museum
results.content: Five years after France returned 26 looted artifacts to Benin, the West African nation has formally requested the repatriation of 35 others.

results.title: Bhutan: Traditional wood painting shapes the kingdom's architecture
results.content: In Bhutan, artisans hand-paint intricate patterns on wooden buildings, preserving a centuries-old tradition. Known as Shing Tshon, the craft remains central to the kingdom's cultural identity.

results.title: Somali protesters come out in support of expulsion of UAE ambassador
results.content: The president accused the UAE of supporting armed forces outside federal control and failing to respect Somalia’s sovereignty.

results.title: One in four children lived in conflict zones in 2025, Save the Children warns
results.content: Save the Children warns that the situation could deteriorate further in 2026, as fighting continues across the Middle East, including Iran, Lebanon and Yemen.

results.title: US: Protesters demand human control over AI after Anthropic's IPO
results.content: Protesters gathered outside Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters on 19 November 2026 to demand tighter regulation and greater human control over artificial intelligence, following the company’s $2 trillion stock market debut.

results.title: Japan: The dark secret behind an island paradise full of rabbits
results.content: Hundreds of rabbits roam freely on Japan's Okunoshima Island, delighting visitors from around the world. But behind its idyllic scenery lies a troubling history of secret chemical weapons production.

results.title: Ukraine: Kyiv metro stations become overnight shelters amid air raids
results.content: Residents of Kyiv, Ukraine, sought refuge in underground metro stations overnight on Thursday 19 November 2026, as repeated air raid alerts warned of further Russian attacks on the capital. Strikes on the Ukrainian capital killed at least one person, injured five and damaged two embassies.

results.title: US national cyber director ousted following wave of tech outages
results.content: His ousting comes as the administration faces fierce criticism over its response to a series of disruptions over the past week.

results.title: Morocco, Senegal, and Mali headline Friday’s U-17 World Cup action
results.content: More than eight matches are scheduled for Friday, including games with African teams Morocco, Côte d’Ivoire, Senegal, and Mali.

results.title: Heavy fighting in Haiti as armed forces battle gangs in capital
results.content: They have been trying to remove powerful gangs that have been long entrenched in a key corridor connecting Port-au-Prince to other regions.

results.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes damage Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv
results.content: Russian strikes damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv on Thursday. Windows were shattered and vehicles damaged, but diplomatic staff escaped unharmed.

results.title: Greenpeace protests at COP31, demands climate finance as island nations face growing threats
results.content: Greenpeace activists are staging a protest at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, demanding urgent action. Small island nations are also raising their voices, warning that the climate crisis threatens their very survival. But Greenpeace says progress at the negotiations remains far too slow.

results.title: 48 teams, 104 matches: FIFA U-17 World Cup kicks off in Qatar
results.content: Qatar is hosting the FIFA U-17 Men’s World Cup, which kicked off on 19 November 2026. It is the second time the country has staged the tournament, following its first hosting in 2025.

results.title: Uganda start U17 World Cup campaign with 3-0 defeat to South Korea
results.content: Uganda’s Under-17 side, the Uganda Cranes, opened their Group B campaign with a 3-0 defeat to South Korea on Thursday.

results.title: Zimbabwe destroys 250,000 landmines, but funding threatens 2030 clearance goal
results.content: A major milestone in Zimbabwe's efforts to clear deadly remnants of war. The HALO Trust, the world's largest landmine clearance charity, says it has destroyed 250,000 landmines across the country since 2013.
